name: PANAMA

flag.title: Flag of Panamá
flag.note: Four quarters: red, white, blue, white

lead: Panama is a skinny, S-shaped country that joins North and South America like a bridge. Its famous Canal cuts 13,000 km off a ship's trip. Giant locks lift ships like bathtubs. Rainforests and nearly 1,000 bird species make it wild.

sections.animals: A jungle full of wild wonders

geo: Thick rainforest covers half of Panama, fed by over 3 m of rain a year. Volcán Barú, the country's only volcano, rises to 3,475 m.
The Canal cuts 80 km across the isthmus, a thin strip of land. Ships skip the long trip around South America. Lakes keep the locks full.
animals: Each autumn, billions of raptors (hunting birds) fly over Panama City. The harpy eagle, the Americas' most powerful bird of prey, nests in remote jungle.
Sloths doze in trees along the Canal. Jaguars prowl Darién. The golden frog is Panama's national symbol, but a deadly fungus means most now live in zoos.
culture: Spanish, West African, Chinese, Indian and Guna people all shaped Panama. The Guna sew bright mola cloth. Patacones (fried plantain) sit beside ceviche and sancocho soup.
Salsa, reggaeton and tamborito drums share one dancefloor. At Carnival each February, women twirl through Panama City in pollera dresses. Sewing one takes months.
history: People lived here for thousands of years before the Spanish came in 1501. Panama City, founded in 1519, was the first European city on the Pacific.
Panama broke from Colombia in 1903, with US support, so the Canal could be built. Panama took full control of the Canal on 31 December 1999.
wows: Gravity fills the Canal's locks, so no pumps are needed.
The Guna people run their own islands and decide who visits.
Panama uses US dollars, but its balboa coin is worth exactly one dollar.
Panama hats are really made in Ecuador, not Panama.
The 2016 Canal expansion lets ships carry ten times the 1914 load: 14,000 containers.
Panama is smaller than Scotland yet has nearly 1,000 bird species.
From Volcán Barú's summit, you can see the Pacific and the Caribbean at once.

myths.myth: The Panama Canal is a flat ditch at sea level
myths.fact: Ships climb 26 m up to Gatún Lake, cross it, then go back down through locks.

myths.myth: The Canal runs east to west
myths.fact: Panama bends like an S. Ships go north to south, and the Pacific end lies east of the Caribbean end.
